_doc: ⚑ S227 (2026-10-10) — MATCH MADE SIMPLE, Second Thoughts' game on the console on Maya's bed (src/games/matchMade.ts). It REPLACES TIDY there (src/games/tidy.ts and s4_tidy.json stay in the repo, unhooked). Ported from the prototype he approved — Pc_Simulation/2026-screen-prototypes/v2_match_made_simple/match_made_simple_v2.html, his: 'Yes it is very good indeed!' — and every word below is that prototype's `T` object, except where his answers of 2026-10-10 changed it. One verb (swap two, match three), turn-based, no clock. A match of hers clears the programme's coating from ITS COPY of Maya and Junie's picture at the Commons; its counter-match coats one patch back, files what she matched under OLD FILE (the misfile), and sends more recommendations. The score is 99 × the curve and can never pass 99%; after twenty-four matches (or STOP HERE at any time) the programme's frame breaks and what is left is the original, untouched: nothing in the game ever wrote to it. The satire is the SELLER's (law of the games: 'a rhetoric of failure … the queer side always wins').
_docRulings: His answers on v2 (2026-10-10), applied in the port: (1) the Commons picture has NO string lights or lanterns — a starry sky instead (his standing preference); (2) the programme's counter-move MAY re-coat Maya's and Junie's faces — 'it increases the challenge and it is a poetic reference' — kept as the prototype does it; (3) their looks are kept as drawn; (4) L's lines are kept, 'YOU CAN ALWAYS GO BACK.' and 'ALMOST BACK TO BEFORE!' (the seller's conversion rhetoric, which collapses at the end); (5) the end card's 99% is a hand-drawn numeral (big, bold pixel digits drawn as shapes) instead of the 5×7 glyphs at 12× — so `limit` below is no longer drawn as text; it names what the numeral says.
_docPort: What the port changed beyond his answers, and why: the console has no M key, so the menu help no longer offers one; its SOUND row is the console's own (it quiets this game and nothing else — the piece's one mute lives in the frame) and shows OFF when either is off. The filing is one line per GAME, not per run (his ruling, per game, not per round).
lCounter: FILED IT IN YOUR OLD FILE!
end2: THE ORIGINAL IS ALL WE FOUND.

_docFiling: Filed once per game, when its first run ends (DeviceGame.takeFiling; ledger.games, id 'matchmade'); never drawn on the console. The record reads it in 2026.
